strings.name: Dawn Song
strings.summary: Dawn Song studies computer-system security, privacy and AI security. She is a UC Berkeley professor and co-director of its Center for Responsible Decentralized Intelligence. Her work brings program analysis, cryptography and machine learning to security research, including collaborative model evaluations such as DecodingTrust. She studies vulnerabilities and defenses; team papers and evaluations do not guarantee the safety of every system or later model.
strings.coverageNote: Reviewed through November 17, 2026. Birth date remains unverified; ACM fellowship uses the 2019 class. Meta personnel changes are attributed to reporting: June hiring does not prove continuing employment, and no individual departure date is inferred.
strings.influence.rationale: Researches computer security, privacy and machine-learning security, advancing trustworthy AI and protection of data use.
strings.facts.f1.label: Education
strings.facts.f1.value: Earned a Tsinghua bachelor’s in 1996, Carnegie Mellon master’s in 1999 and Berkeley doctorate in 2002.
strings.facts.f2.label: Research roles
strings.facts.f2.value: UC Berkeley computer science professor and co-director of the Center for Responsible Decentralized Intelligence (RDI).
strings.highlights.h1.title: System security and privacy
strings.highlights.h1.text: Studies software, network and distributed-system security, combining program analysis and cryptography to explore defenses.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Language-model trustworthiness
strings.highlights.h2.text: Co-authored DecodingTrust, evaluating bias, privacy and adversarial robustness in GPT models of that period.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Meta team departures reported
strings.timeline.t1.text: Semafor reports Meta is dismissing June’s Virtue AI hires, whose joining group included Song.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Co-authored paper receives Test of Time award
strings.timeline.t2.text: RSAC honors the 2002 homomorphic-signatures paper by Robert Johnson, David Molnar, Dawn Song and David Wagner.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Elected to American Academy of Arts and Sciences
strings.timeline.t3.text: Berkeley confirms her election; this academy is distinct from the American Association for the Advancement of Science.
strings.timeline.t4.title: DecodingTrust wins paper award
strings.timeline.t4.text: NeurIPS announces the collaboration’s Outstanding Paper award in the Datasets and Benchmarks track’s benchmark category; she is a co-author.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Berkeley announces ACM fellowship
strings.timeline.t5.text: Berkeley confirms her selection for the 2019 class for security and privacy contributions, taking precedence over her homepage’s 2020 listing.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Receives MacArthur Fellowship
strings.timeline.t6.text: The foundation announces her inclusion in its 2010 class, recognizing computer-security research.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Joins Berkeley faculty
strings.timeline.t7.text: Moves to Berkeley after teaching at Carnegie Mellon from 2002 to 2007.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Earns Berkeley doctorate
strings.timeline.t8.text: Completes a computer science doctorate; Berkeley’s fellowship profile names Doug Tygar as her advisor.
